subject: Clarify cloud-carveout / KMS responsibility and bridge letter for CensusBridge SOC2
messages:
From: Daniel Burns <d.burns@censusbridge.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@censusbridge.com
Date: Wed, 3 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 coverage question — cloud carve-out & KMS ownership

Marcus — thanks for taking this. We're preparing for our SOC 2 Type II and the auditors asked for confirmation of subservice carve-outs for providers like Redwood. A couple quick asks so we can map responsibilities correctly: 

1) For customers of Redwood Private/Dedicated, do you carve out cloud provider responsibilities (networking, hypervisor, physical access) from your SOC 2? If so, do you have a standard carve-out statement we can reference?

2) KMS / key custody: our compliance team needs to know whether Redwood treats KMS as a subservice (i.e., you rely on cloud provider KMS attestation) or if Redwood manages key custody on behalf of the customer. If you rely on the provider's KMS, would you be comfortable providing a bridge letter or subservice mapping that lists the relevant cloud provider SOC 2 report and the control coverage for encryption/crypto key management?

3) Audit period coverage: can you confirm the typical audit period (calendar year or rolling 12 months) you include in your SOC 2 reports and whether you can provide a short statement if we need coverage aligned to our audit window (which is 2024-10-01 to 2025-09-30).

We're trying to produce a clear dependency map for our auditors — if it helps we can share the auditor contact directly. Appreciate any docs/evidence you can share.

— Daniel
Security & Privacy, CensusBridge

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Burns <d.burns@censusbridge.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Sep 2025 12:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 coverage question — cloud carve-out & KMS ownership

Hi Daniel — thanks for laying this out. Quick answers and we're happy to follow with formal artifacts. I've looped in Lauren (legal/partner ops) and Neha (compliance) for details and attachments. Summary below: 

1) Carve-outs: Redwood's standard SOC 2 report treats the underlying cloud provider as a subservice organization for infrastructure-level controls (physical security, hypervisor, network fabric). We provide a dependency mapping that lists which controls are carved out and reference the provider's SOC 2 report and relevant bridge language. We do not carve out application-level responsibilities (RBAC, config, application logging) — those remain in-scope.

2) KMS/key custody: For our Hosted and Dedicated offering, we use customer-managed keys in supported setups; when customers opt for Redwood-managed keys (default for quick onboarding), we rely on the cloud provider's KMS and its SOC 2 coverage for the cryptographic key management controls. For Private/on-prem instances where the customer supplies keys, Redwood does not have custody.

Given your auditor window (2024-10-01 — 2025-09-30), we can: 
- Provide our SOC 2 Type II report covering the same-ish period, plus a bridge letter that states reliance on the cloud provider SOC 2 for KMS and physical controls.
- Provide the list of subprocessors and the latest cloud provider SOC 2 reference (we maintain the mapping in our compliance drive).

Neha — can you confirm the exact artifacts we'll share and whether we need a tailored attestation to match CensusBridge's audit dates? Lauren — if there's any legal attestation language we avoid, flag it.

Thanks — Marcus
VP, Platform Security (on behalf of Redwood Inference)

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Burns <d.burns@censusbridge.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Sep 2025 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 coverage question — cloud carve-out & KMS ownership

Daniel — following up with the artifacts we can provide and a short checklist so your auditors can reconcile items quickly. Attaching a stub list below; I'll upload formal PDFs to our secure share once Marcus confirms. 

Deliverables we can provide today/this week: 
- Redwood Inference SOC 2 Type II report (standard audit window; PDF).
- Bridge letter template that references the cloud provider SOC 2 specifically for physical security, network, and KMS (we will include an explicit statement of which controls we consider subservice).
- Cloud provider SOC 2 reference (we link to the provider's attestation and include the report name and period).
- Subprocessor inventory CSV (current as of today).
- Mapping table that ties Redwood controls to your auditor's control IDs (if you provide their control list we can map).

One important note: we are careful about wording that implies the provider's report covers application-level encryption design or Redwood's operational key-handling procedures. The bridge letter will state "Redwood relies on the cloud provider for physical & infrastructure-level controls, including KMS as configured by Redwood; Redwood remains responsible for application-level configuration and access controls."

Next steps: Marcus — if you confirm we should produce a bridge letter tailored to CensusBridge's audit dates, I'll prepare a draft. Daniel — please tell us the auditor contact or confirm whether a standard bridge letter + AWS SOC 2 (attached) will suffice.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Director, Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment (stub): redwood-soc2-2024-stub.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Daniel Burns <d.burns@censusbridge.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@censusbridge.com
Date: Wed, 10 Sep 2025 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 coverage question — cloud carve-out & KMS ownership

Thanks Marcus / Neha — this is helpful. For timing we need coverage aligned exactly with our window (2024-10-01 through 2025-09-30). If you can provide: 

- A tailored bridge letter mentioning that Redwood's SOC 2 report covers application-level controls for the listed periods and that KMS/infrastructure is a subservice (explicitly reference the cloud provider SOC 2 and the report date range).
- The cloud provider SOC 2 PDF and a current subprocessor list (CSV).

Those two items should satisfy our auditor. I'm attaching the cloud provider report (AWS) and our current subprocessor export for your records. We're not asking Redwood to assert AWS controls beyond what's in their report — just to confirm the dependency mapping and call out the exact audit windows.

I'll accept the draft bridge letter via email; if you'd prefer a DocuSign flow for a signed attestation we can provide a link. Thank you — we'll route to our auditor after receipt.

— Daniel
Security & Privacy, CensusBridge

Attachments (stubs): aws-soc2-2024.pdf (application/pdf), censusbridge-subprocessors-20250910.csv (text/csv)
